subject: Large difference between the outcome of MCMC run by (compileNimble-> runMCMC) and MCMCsuite

messages.author: 4364ce565c0e42d1
messages.subject: Large difference between the outcome of MCMC run by (compileNimble-> runMCMC) and MCMCsuite
parts:
Hey all, 
I have been dealing with a very strange situation that I really don't know how to explain it, hoping I could borrow some brain power from here. 

The problem is that I have a very simple model which I try to take sample from a multivariate normal with specified mean and cov. However, the cov has a lots of zero elements in it and I'm hoping following the MCMC the simulated variables also keep those zero and near zero values in their cov.

So I compared the simulated outcomes for the same model, data and initial conditions once by compiling it and once with MCMCSuite. The difference is unbelievable. The one that is compiled is very unstable and it's doing much worse in simulating cov s (in upper diagonal matrix) in order of couple of 1000 whereas the MCMCSuite is much closer to zero.

Any thoughts or ideas ?

You can find the code and the outcomes here: http://rpubs.com/Para2x/464195

messages.subject: Re: Large difference between the outcome of MCMC run by (compileNimble-> runMCMC) and MCMCsuite
parts:
Thanks so much for raising this concern, Hamze.  The short story, I'm pleased to say, is there's no discrepancy between the result from runMCMC() and MCMCsuite().

The very short reason for what you observed, is a slight difference in handling of (the interplay between) burnin, and thinning, in runMCMC() as compared to MCMCsuite().  I'll also mention that NIMBLE gives an informative message along these lines, when you use runMCMC(), and include *both* a non-zero burnin, and thinning interval > 1.  This message, which was suppressed in the Rpubs document you published, looks like:

samples.list <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, niter = 5e6, nburnin=1e3, nchains = 2, thin=500)
## runMCMC's handling of nburnin changed in nimble version 0.6-11. Previously, nburnin samples were discarded *post-thinning*.  Now nburnin samples are discarded *pre-thinning*.  The number of samples returned will be floor((niter-nburnin)/thin).

If you read this carefully, and/or the documentation for runMCMC() and MCMCsuite() which explains the same thing, then here's the difference:

runMCMC() does burnin *pre-thinning*, so in your case, the number of samples being recorded was:
floor(niter-nburnin)/thin) = floor((5000000 - 1000) / 500) = 9998

Note that in your Rpubs document, MCMCsuite was only being run for 2e6 MCMC iterations, different from the run for runMCMC(),

MCMCsuite() uses older behaviour, where burnin is done *post-thinning*, so the number of samples being recorded was:
floor(niter / thin) - nburnin = floor(2000000 / 500) - 1000 = 4000 - 1000 = 3000

At the end of the day, these differences in the number of samples being executed, and recorded, was giving rise to the discrepancy you noticed.

I've gone ahead and modified your code slightly, just to demonstrate the agreement.  Please look carefully at the comments included, to see the changes I've made (using set.seed(), changing to 1 chain only, executing the same number of samples for each, removing the thinning, and perhaps others).

Thanks again for posting this, and keep in touch with any further questions.

Cheers,
Daniel
for the NIMBLE development team


library(nimble)

Pf <- matrix(c(4729.4, 236.58, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 
 236.6,  46.49, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 0.000e+00, 
   0.0,   0.00, 4.850e+03, 5.205e+02, 6.785e-59, 7.285e-60, 
   0.0,   0.00, 5.205e+02, 1.310e+02, 7.283e-60, 1.829e-60, 
   0.0,   0.00, 6.785e-59, 7.283e-60, 4.850e+03, 5.207e+02, 
   0.0,   0.00, 7.285e-60, 1.829e-60, 5.207e+02, 1.312e+02), nrow=6)

mu.f <- c(156.69,  17.29, 192.87,  18.98, 192.87,  18.98)

multiVarCode <- nimbleCode({
    X.mod[1:6] ~ dmnorm(mean = muf[1:6], cov = pf[1:6, 1:6])
})


data.tobit <- list(muf = as.vector(mu.f), pf = Pf)

inits.pred <- list(X.mod = as.vector(mu.f))

model_pred <- nimbleModel(multiVarCode,
                          data = data.tobit,
                          inits = inits.pred,
                          name = 'base')

conf <- configureMCMC(model_pred, print=TRUE)

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(model_pred)

Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project=model_pred)

set.seed(0)  ## NEW

## REMOVED samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE
## only running one chain: nchains = 1
## *** no longer using any thinning ***
samples.list <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, niter = 5e6, nburnin=1e3, nchains = 1) ###, thin=500)
## runMCMC's handling of nburnin changed in nimble version 0.6-11. Previously, nburnin samples were discarded *post-thinning*.  Now nburnin samples are discarded *pre-thinning*.  The number of samples returned will be floor((niter-nburnin)/thin).
